production.waterSource: The distillery uses water from the Glenmore spring to reduce new make spirit to 63.5% ABV before cask filling; the Glenmore river supplies cooling water.
production.fermentation: Ardnamurchan uses seven washbacks in total: four wooden washbacks, comprising one oak and three Oregon pine, plus three stainless-steel washbacks.
production.stills: The distillery uses traditional copper pot stills: a 10,000-litre wash still and a 6,000-litre spirit still. The spirit still has a boil ball for additional reflux, and both stills feed standard shell-and-tube condensers located outside the building. Heating is by steam generated from a local woodchip biomass boiler.
production.peat: The distillery describes its intended house profile as showing gentle peat smoke rather than a heavily peated style.
production.maturation: Ardnamurchan matures whisky on site in its own dunnage warehouses on the Ardnamurchan peninsula, close to the North Atlantic.

houseCharacter: Ardnamurchan's mixed wooden and stainless-steel washback regime gives the distillery flexibility in how fermentation-derived character is developed, while the exact fermentation duration is not stated in the verified source set. The spirit still's boil ball increases reflux, and external shell-and-tube condensers support a clean but still weighty spirit structure. On-site dunnage maturation preserves a close link between production and maturation, supporting the distillery's stated gently smoky, rich, oily, honeyed and fruity house direction.
cask23Narrative: Ardnamurchan combines modern engineering with a deliberately traditional maturation setup. Its spirit still uses a boil ball to encourage extra reflux, while both wooden and stainless-steel washbacks are used in fermentation and the whisky matures in dunnage warehouses beside the distillery. The result is a West Highland style built around gentle peat, oiliness, honeyed fruit and coastal character rather than aggressive smoke.
